name: Plastic
tips: Rinse and dry plastic bottles before disposal.
Crush plastic bottles to save space in the recycling bin.
Check recycling resin identification code (1 to 7) at the bottom.
description: Thermoplastics and recyclables including PET bottles, HDPE jugs, containers, and packaging material.

name: Paper
tips: Keep paper dry and free of food oil or grease.
Flatten cardboard boxes before putting them in the bin.
Remove plastic tape and metallic staples where possible.
description: Newspapers, corrugated boxes, office stationery, brochures, and paper cartons.

name: Glass
tips: Remove metal caps and corks before recycling.
Wrap broken glass carefully in thick newspaper to protect sanitation workers.
Glass can be recycled indefinitely without loss in purity.
description: Glass jars, beverage bottles, cosmetic glass containers, and cullet.

name: Metal
tips: Rinse food cans to avoid attracting pests.
Aluminum soda cans are 100% recyclable and save massive energy.
Separate iron/steel from aluminum if sending to scrap dealers (kabadiwala).
description: Aluminum beverage cans, tin food cans, foil trays, metal caps, and clean scrap metals.

name: Organic
tips: Never mix plastic wrap or polythene with wet kitchen waste.
Compost vegetable peels, tea leaves, and garden trimmings at home.
Do not add cooked oily leftovers in large quantities to simple vermicompost bins.
description: Fruit & vegetable peels, leftover food, tea leaves, garden leaves, and biodegradable waste.

name: E-waste
tips: Never throw electronics in municipal street garbage bins.
Deposit phones, chargers, and circuit boards at authorized EPR take-back points.
Tape battery terminals to prevent short-circuits and fire hazard.
description: Old mobile phones, chargers, laptops, wires, PCB boards, consumer electronics, and peripherals.

name: Hazardous
tips: Wrap sanitary pads and diapers in newspaper or marked red pouches.
Store expired medicines and chemical bottles separately from everyday trash.
Do not puncture aerosol cans or incinerate chemical containers.
description: Batteries, paint cans, pesticides, expired medicines, medical needles, sanitaries, and chemicals.

name: Textile
tips: Donate usable clothes to charities or NGOs like Goonj.
Repurpose worn-out cotton tees into household dusting rags.
Send torn synthetic fabrics to specialized textile fiber recovery units.
description: Discarded garments, bed linens, torn fabric scraps, footwear, and curtains.

name: Other
tips: Try to minimize mixed non-recyclables like multi-layer chips packets.
Ensure ash, ceramic fragments, and street sweepings are kept dry.
Use as RDF (Refuse Derived Fuel) or send to scientific municipal landfills.
description: Multi-layer laminate packaging, broken ceramics, dust, composite materials, and general inert refuse.
